name: Zedekiah
charge: Breaking his oath to Nebuchadnezzar; stiffening his neck against the Lord's word by Jeremiah
summary: Sworn by God to serve Babylon, Zedekiah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar and would not humble himself before Jeremiah speaking from the mouth of the Lord. Warned to the last that surrender would save the city and his life, he feared the Jews who had defected more than he feared the word.
offense: Zedekiah did evil and would not humble himself before Jeremiah. He also rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. Ezekiel exposed the broken covenant through the figure of the vine that turned toward another eagle, seeking Egyptian help. The oath was not made harmless by the fact that it had been sworn to a foreign king. Jeremiah told Zedekiah that surrender would preserve his life and prevent the city from being burned. Zedekiah feared that the Jews who had already fallen to the Chaldeans would abuse him. The prophet assured him that they would not and urged him to obey. The king nevertheless refused the way of escape set before him.
judgment: The city was besieged until famine prevailed. Zedekiah fled by night, but the Chaldeans overtook him in the plains of Jericho and brought him to Riblah. His sons were killed before his eyes; then his eyes were put out, and he was bound and taken to Babylon. Jerusalem was burned as Jeremiah had warned. The king who feared the humiliation of surrender suffered a far greater calamity through resistance. God's warning had included mercy, but Zedekiah would not submit to receive it.

verses.text: Zedekiah was one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord his God, and humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord.
And he also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God: but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart from turning unto the Lord God of Israel.

And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it; and they built forts against it round about.
And the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
And on the ninth day of the fourth month the famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

And the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls, which is by the king’s garden: (now the Chaldees were against the city round about:) and the king went the way toward the plain.
And the army of the Chaldees pursued after the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army were scattered from him.
So they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him.
And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.
And king Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, did hearken unto the words of the Lord, which he spake by the prophet Jeremiah.

Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon’s princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house:

But if thou wilt not go forth to the king of Babylon’s princes, then shall this city be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.
And Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me.
But Jeremiah said, They shall not deliver thee. Obey, I beseech thee, the voice of the Lord, which I speak unto thee: so it shall be well unto thee, and thy soul shall live.
But if thou refuse to go forth, this is the word that the Lord hath shewed me:

And, behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judah’s house shall be brought forth to the king of Babylon’s princes, and those women shall say, Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back.

So they shall bring out all thy wives and thy children to the Chaldeans: and thou shalt not escape out of their hand, but shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon: and thou shalt cause this city to be burned with fire.
But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
Then they took the king, and carried him up unto the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; where he gave judgment upon him.
And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah.
Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death.

Say now to the rebellious house, Know ye not what these things mean? tell them, Behold, the king of Babylon is come to Jerusalem, and hath taken the king thereof, and the princes thereof, and led them with him to Babylon;
And hath taken of the king’s seed, and made a covenant with him, and hath taken an oath of him: he hath also taken the mighty of the land:
That the kingdom might be base, that it might not lift itself up, but that by keeping of his covenant it might stand.

But he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and much people. Shall he prosper? shall he escape that doeth such things? or shall he break the covenant, and be delivered?
As I live, saith the Lord God, surely in the place where the king dwelleth that made him king, whose oath he despised, and whose covenant he brake, even with him in the midst of Babylon he shall die.
Neither shall Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company make for him in the war, by casting up mounts, and building forts, to cut off many persons:
Seeing he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, lo, he had given his hand, and hath done all these things, he shall not escape.
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; As I live, surely mine oath that he hath despised, and my covenant that he hath broken, even it will I recompense upon his own head.
And thou, profane wicked prince of Israel, whose day is come, when iniquity shall have an end,
Thus saith the Lord God; Remove the diadem, and take off the crown: this shall not be the same: exalt him that is low, and abase him that is high.
I will overturn, overturn, overturn, it: and it shall be no more, until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him.

entries.commentary: The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and make him king in Jerusalem; he is twenty three years old and reigns three months. The king of Egypt puts him down, condemns the land in a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold, and makes Eliakim his brother king, turning his name to Jehoiakim, and carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

Jehoiakim is twenty five years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord his God, so Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar also carries off the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and puts them in his temple. The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time. -

Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord. When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

Zedekiah is twenty one years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years, and he does evil in the sight of the Lord his God and humbles not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God, and stiffens his neck and hardens his heart from turning to the Lord God of Israel. The chief priests and people transgress very much after all the abominations of the heathen and pollute the house of the Lord. The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy. -

The Most High brings upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slays their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and has no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man or him that stooped for age. He gives them all into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, and all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes are brought to Babylon. They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of. -

Those who escape the sword are carried away to Babylon, where they are servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia. This fulfills the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, that the land would enjoy her sabbaths and lie desolate to fulfill threescore and ten years.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom. Cyrus declares that the Lord God of heaven has given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and calls any of the Lord's people to go up, showing again that the Most High sets over the earth one that is profitable for his purpose. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign Nebuchadnezzar came with all his host against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about it. The city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, and the famine prevailed in the city. Because the city was besieged no food, water, or goods could get in, so there was no bread for the people of the land.

The city was broken up and the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were round about the city. The army pursued the king, overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and his army was scattered from him, and they took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was given upon him. They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon, just as Jeremiah had warned him.

In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem. He burnt the house of the Lord, the king's house, and every great man's house, and the army broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about. He carried away the rest of the people and the fugitives, but left the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen, since the poor could not fend for themselves.

The Chaldeans broke in pieces the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried the brass to Babylon because it was valuable. They took away the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and vessels of brass, and the firepans and bowls of gold and silver the captain of the guard took away. The two pillars, one sea, and the bases Solomon had made were of brass without weight, the one pillar eighteen cubits high with a brasen chapiter, wreathen work, and pomegranates round about.

The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door. He took an officer over the men of war, five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and threescore men of the people found in the city. Nebuzaradan brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and the king smote and slew them there; so Judah was carried away out of their land.

Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor. Gedaliah counselled the captains and their men not to fear to serve the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them. But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and the people fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, killing a man who gave wise counsel.

In the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison and spake kindly to him. He set his throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and let him eat bread continually before him all the days of his life. Jehoiachin was given a continual daily allowance for the rest of his life, a mercy shown at the very end of the account. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

King Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigns in place of Coniah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in the land of Judah, but neither he nor his servants nor the people hearken to the words of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah. Zedekiah sends men to ask Jeremiah to pray to the Most High for them, while Jeremiah is still going in and out among the people, not yet put into prison. Pharaoh's army comes out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem hear of it, they depart from the city.

The word of the Most High comes to Jeremiah for the king of Judah: Pharaoh's army that came to help shall return to Egypt into their own land. The Chaldeans shall come again, fight against this city, take it, and burn it with fire; the people are not to deceive themselves that the Chaldeans have surely departed. Even if they smote the whole Chaldean army so that only wounded men remained, those men would rise up in their tents and burn the city with fire.

When the Chaldean army breaks up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army, Jeremiah goes forth toward the land of Benjamin to separate himself among the people. At the gate of Benjamin a captain of the ward named Irijah seizes him, charging that he is falling away to the Chaldeans; Jeremiah answers that it is false, but Irijah will not hear him. Irijah brings Jeremiah to the princes, who are wroth with him, smite him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe.

After Jeremiah has remained many days in the dungeon and its cells, Zedekiah secretly sends for him and asks if there is any word from the Most High; Jeremiah answers there is, that the king shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon. Jeremiah asks what he has offended against the king, his servants, or the people that they have put him in prison, and where now are the prophets who prophesied that the king of Babylon would not come. He pleads not to be sent back to the house of Jonathan the scribe lest he die there; Zedekiah commands he be kept in the court of the prison and given a daily piece of bread out of the bakers' street until all the bread in the city is spent.

Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashur hear Jeremiah telling the people that whoever remains in the city shall die by sword, famine, and pestilence, but whoever goes forth to the Chaldeans shall live and have his life for a prey. The princes tell the king that Jeremiah must be put to death because he weakens the hands of the men of war and seeks not the welfare of the people but their hurt; the king answers that he is in their hand and the king can do nothing against them. They cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah in the court of the prison, letting him down with cords into a place with no water but mire, and Jeremiah sinks in the mire.

Abedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's house, hears that Jeremiah has been put in the dungeon while the king sits in the gate of Benjamin. Abedmelech goes to the king and says these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah, who is likely to die of hunger where he is, for there is no more bread in the city; the king commands him to take thirty men and lift the prophet out before he dies. Abedmelech takes old cast clouts and rotten rags, lets them down by cords, and tells Jeremiah to put them under his armholes under the cords; they draw him up out of the dungeon, and Jeremiah remains in the court of the prison.

Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah into the third entry of the house of the Most High and asks him to hide nothing; Jeremiah answers that if he declares it the king will surely put him to death, and if he counsels him the king will not hearken. The king swears secretly that as the Most High liveth he will not put him to death nor give him into the hand of those who seek his life. Jeremiah tells him that if he goes forth to the king of Babylon's princes his soul shall live and the city shall not be burned, but if he will not go forth the city shall be given to the Chaldeans and burned; the king says he is afraid of the Jews already fallen to the Chaldeans, and Jeremiah urges him to obey the voice of the Most High that it may be well with him.

If the king refuses to go forth, Jeremiah shows him that all the women left in the king's house shall be brought out to the king of Babylon's princes, saying his friends have prevailed against him and his feet are sunk in the mire and turned away back. All his wives and children shall be brought to the Chaldeans, and he shall not escape but be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon and cause the city to be burned with fire. Zedekiah charges Jeremiah to let no man know their words, and to tell the princes only that he presented his supplication not to be returned to Jonathan's house; the princes come and ask, Jeremiah answers as the king commanded, and he abides in the court of the prison until the day Jerusalem is taken.

Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and his mother was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. Zedekiah was not of the royal lineage per se, and Zedekiah was not really his name; to see how he became king we go back to when Babylon took the real king away. -

He did that which was evil in the eyes of the Most High as Jehoiakim had done, and through the anger of the Most High against Jerusalem and Judah, Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. The Most High had told through Jeremiah that the people would have to serve Babylon seventy years, but Zedekiah decided to rebel against it instead of submitting to the prophecy. -

In the ninth year of his reign Nebuchadnezzar and all his army came against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about, and the city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah. By the fourth month the famine was so sore in the city that there was no bread for the people of the land. This should sound familiar; the same siege and famine came on us again under the Romans in 70 A.D. These are generational curses that fall on multiple generations when we break the Most High's commandments. -

When the city was broken up the men of war fled by night by the gate between the two walls, but the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, his army scattered from him. They brought Zedekiah to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where he gave judgment upon him, and the king of Babylon slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes and slew all the princes of Judah. Then they put out Zedekiah's eyes, so the last thing he would ever see was his sons put to death in his face, and they bound him in chains, carried him to Babylon, and kept him in prison till the day of his death; the Most High allowed these heathen to bring hell into Jerusalem. -

In the fifth month Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem and burned the house of the Most High, the king's house, and all the houses of the great men with fire. The Chaldeans birthed this destruction, but Edom, the so-called white man, took part in it; Esau loves burning things, which is ironic since he is destined to burn forever, wasted away by the same fire he loved to waste these nations with. Edom were Babylon's personal cheerleaders, calling for Jerusalem and the temple to be razed to the foundation; the daughter of Babylon that Edom cheered on became the mother of harlots, Babylon the great, which is to be destroyed. -

Nebuzaradan carried away captive certain of the poor of the people, the residue in the city, and those that had fallen to the king of Babylon, but left certain of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen. The Chaldeans broke the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brazen sea in the house of the Most High and carried all the brass to Babylon, along with the caldrons, shovels, snuffers, bowls, spoons, and every vessel of brass, gold, and silver. This was a billion dollar heist of the temple's gold, brass, and silver, and it too was prophecy; it fulfilled what was foretold to Hezekiah when he foolishly showed Babylon all his treasures. -

The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, the three keepers of the door, the eunuch over the men of war, seven of the king's counselors, the principal scribe, and threescore men of the people found in the city. He brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where the king smote them and put them to death, and thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land. Babylon made sure to put our mighty men to death, the same tactic the oppressor always used in slavery and segregation, killing the mightiest men to destroy the people's hope so they would no longer rise up against the enemy. -

These are the numbers Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year 3,023 Jews, in the eighteenth year 832 persons from Jerusalem, and in the twenty-third year Nebuzaradan carried away 745 persons, four thousand and six hundred in all.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the first year of his reign lifted up his head, brought him out of prison, and spake kindly to him. He set Jehoiachin's throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and gave him a continual daily allowance of food all the days of his life. Jehoiachin was the real king carried captive earlier in Second Kings 24, and after his long imprisonment he found favor; his lineage became the line through which Christ came. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The word of the Most High came to Ezekiel to put forth a riddle and speak a parable unto the house of Israel. A great eagle with great wings and divers colors came unto Lebanon, took the highest branch of the cedar, cropped off the top of his young twigs, and carried it into a land of traffic and a city of merchants. He took also of the seed of the land, planted it in a fruitful field by great waters, and it grew into a spreading vine of low stature whose branches turned toward him.

There was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers, and this vine bent her roots and shot forth her branches toward him that he might water it, though it was already planted in good soil by great waters. The Most High asks whether it shall prosper; He shall pull up the roots and cut off the fruit that it wither, and when the east wind touches it, it shall utterly wither in the furrows where it grew.

The Most High tells the rebellious house what these things mean: the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took the king and princes to Babylon, took of the king's seed, made a covenant and took an oath of him, and also took the mighty of the land. The enemy takes the mighty of the land, the best and brightest, and turns them against their people by giving them the mind of the oppressor, so the kingdom might be base and not lift itself up. When our people do well financially, get a good education, and buy into the pick-yourself-up-by-the-bootstraps idea that everyone has the same opportunity, the smart ones are removed from the ghetto so they will not be there to cause the uprising. -

The king rebelled against Babylon and sent ambassadors into Egypt for horses and much people; the Most High asks shall he prosper, shall he escape, or shall he break the covenant and be delivered. Because he despised the oath and broke the covenant after giving his hand, he shall die in the midst of Babylon, and Pharaoh with his mighty army shall not help him in the war. The Most High will spread His net upon him, take him in His snare, bring him to Babylon, and plead with him there; his fugitives shall fall by the sword and the remnant be scattered, and they shall know that He is the Lord.

The Most High will Himself take of the highest branch of the high cedar, crop off a tender twig, and plant it upon the high mountain in the height of Israel. It shall bring forth boughs, bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar under which all fowl of every wing shall dwell, and all the trees of the field shall know that He has brought down the high tree and exalted the low tree. If the Most High has declared it, it shall come to pass, for the scripture cannot be broken. -

The word of the Most High comes to Ezekiel to set his face toward Jerusalem, drop his word toward the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel. The Most High is against her and will draw forth His sword out of his sheath to cut off the righteous and the wicked, the sword being the nations He sends. He judges us as a nation, so the righteous and the wicked all get judged together; the sword goes forth against all flesh from the south to the north and shall not return.

Ezekiel is told to sigh with the breaking of his loins and with bitterness before their eyes. When they ask why he sighs he is to answer that it is for the tidings that come, because every heart shall melt, all hands be feeble, every spirit faint, and all knees be weak as water.

A sword is sharpened and furbished, meaning polished, sharpened to make a sore slaughter and furbished that it may glitter. It contemneth the rod of His son, and Judah is that rod; the sword is given to be furbished into the hand of the slayer. Ezekiel is to cry and howl, for the sword shall be upon His people and upon all the princes of Israel; it is a trial, a sword that has already been tested by other nations that the Lord uses.

Ezekiel is to smite his hands together and let the sword be doubled the third time, the sword of the slain that enters even into their private chambers so there is no escape. The point of the sword is set against all their gates, and that point is Babylon pointing at all the gates of Jerusalem. The sword goes one way or the other, to the right hand or the left, whichever way it turns to seek judgment and destruction upon Jerusalem, and the Most High's fury shall rest there.

The word of the Most High comes again to appoint two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come, both out of one land. One way points to Rabbath of the Ammonites and the other to Judah in fenced Jerusalem, and the king of Babylon stands at the parting of the ways to use divination, which is witchcraft. He makes his arrows bright, consults with images, and looks in the liver, and at his right hand the divination points for Jerusalem to appoint captains and set battering rams against the gates.

Because their iniquity is remembered and their transgressions discovered so that their sins appear, they shall be taken with the hand. To the profane wicked prince of Israel whose day is come, He says remove the diadem and take off the crown, exalt him that is low and abase him that is high. He will overturn, overturn, overturn it, and it shall be no more until he come whose right it is, and He will give it to him.

Concerning the Ammonites and their reproach, the sword is drawn and furbished to consume because of the glittering. While the diviners see vanity and divine a lie, the sword will bring them upon the necks of the slain whose day is come. He will judge them in the place where they were created, in the land of their nativity, pour out His indignation, blow against them in the fire of His wrath, and deliver them into the hand of brutish men skilful to destroy; they shall be for fuel to the fire and be no more remembered.

text.text: Zedekiah was one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord his God, and humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord.
And he also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God: but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart from turning unto the Lord God of Israel.

And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it; and they built forts against it round about.
And the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
And on the ninth day of the fourth month the famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

And the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls, which is by the king’s garden: (now the Chaldees were against the city round about:) and the king went the way toward the plain.
And the army of the Chaldees pursued after the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army were scattered from him.
So they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him.
And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.
And king Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, did hearken unto the words of the Lord, which he spake by the prophet Jeremiah.

Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon’s princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house:

But if thou wilt not go forth to the king of Babylon’s princes, then shall this city be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.
And Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me.
But Jeremiah said, They shall not deliver thee. Obey, I beseech thee, the voice of the Lord, which I speak unto thee: so it shall be well unto thee, and thy soul shall live.
But if thou refuse to go forth, this is the word that the Lord hath shewed me:

And, behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judah’s house shall be brought forth to the king of Babylon’s princes, and those women shall say, Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back.

So they shall bring out all thy wives and thy children to the Chaldeans: and thou shalt not escape out of their hand, but shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon: and thou shalt cause this city to be burned with fire.
But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
Then they took the king, and carried him up unto the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; where he gave judgment upon him.
And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah.
Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death.

Say now to the rebellious house, Know ye not what these things mean? tell them, Behold, the king of Babylon is come to Jerusalem, and hath taken the king thereof, and the princes thereof, and led them with him to Babylon;
And hath taken of the king’s seed, and made a covenant with him, and hath taken an oath of him: he hath also taken the mighty of the land:
That the kingdom might be base, that it might not lift itself up, but that by keeping of his covenant it might stand.

But he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and much people. Shall he prosper? shall he escape that doeth such things? or shall he break the covenant, and be delivered?
As I live, saith the Lord God, surely in the place where the king dwelleth that made him king, whose oath he despised, and whose covenant he brake, even with him in the midst of Babylon he shall die.
Neither shall Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company make for him in the war, by casting up mounts, and building forts, to cut off many persons:
Seeing he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, lo, he had given his hand, and hath done all these things, he shall not escape.
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; As I live, surely mine oath that he hath despised, and my covenant that he hath broken, even it will I recompense upon his own head.
And thou, profane wicked prince of Israel, whose day is come, when iniquity shall have an end,
Thus saith the Lord God; Remove the diadem, and take off the crown: this shall not be the same: exalt him that is low, and abase him that is high.
I will overturn, overturn, overturn, it: and it shall be no more, until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him.
